content: It works by promoting the excretion of excess water and salt through the urine. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other purposes. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Methyclothiazide is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically once daily in the morning. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. In addition to its primary uses, methyclothiazide may be prescribed for conditions such as diabetes insipidus, certain electrolyte imbalances, or to prevent kidney stones in individuals with elevated calcium levels in their blood. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of using this medication for your specific condition with your doctor. Before starting methyclothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, sulfa drugs, or any other substances. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or diseases affecting the kidneys, liver, thyroid, or parathyroid glands. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor immediately. Should you become pregnant while taking methyclothiazide, contact your doctor right away. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Be aware that methyclothiazide may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate this drowsiness, so it is advisable to limit alcohol consumption. Additionally, methyclothiazide may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Follow your doctor’s dietary recommendations, which may include a low-salt or low-sodium diet, potassium supplements, or consuming potassium-rich foods such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice. Your doctor may also suggest incorporating a daily exercise routine. If you miss a dose of methyclothiazide, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Common side effects of methyclothiazide include frequent urination (which typically subsides after a few weeks), muscle weakness, dizziness, cramps, thirst, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, headache, and hair loss. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects requiring immediate medical attention include a sore throat accompanied by fever, unusual bleeding or bruising, severe skin rash with peeling, and difficulty breathing or swallowing. If you experience any severe side effects, you or your doctor can report them to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store methyclothiazide in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Methyclothiazide is sold under the brand names Aquatensen® and Enduron®.
